title: Error Reduction for Randomized Logspace
statement: Let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings in randomized logspace, and let $d$ be a nonnegative integer. There exist a constant $c$ and a finite-state randomized Turing machine $M$ using at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ space on inputs $x$ such that, for every $x$, there is a time bound $T$ by which every computation branch halts. If $x\in L$, then $M$ outputs the one-symbol string $[\mathrm{true}]$ with probability at least $1-(1/2)^{(|x|+1)^d}$; if $x\notin L$, then every choice word of length $T$ makes $M$ output $[\mathrm{false}]$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is in randomized logspace, with the one-sided error and space guarantees in the definition of $RL$
